terms.definition: A network of recruiting-focused websites for college football and basketball that rates prospects; it also runs the 247Sports Composite.
An NCAA Division I measure of a team's academic eligibility and retention per term (max 1,000), with penalties for low scores and a 930 multi-year benchmark for postseason eligibility.
A signee who meets a school's admission rules but not the NCAA's core-course GPA standard, so he may get aid and practice but may not play, without losing a year of eligibility.

The NCAA Division I and II model, starting 2026-27, giving up to five years of eligibility that begin at the earlier of first full-time college enrollment or the academic year after the 19th birthday, then run continuously.
terms.variants: NCAA says "5 for 5" is not accurate

terms.definition: The percentage of a roster or recruiting class made up of blue-chip (usually four- and five-star) recruits.

A walk-on the NCAA does not classify as a recruited student-athlete (no official visit, scholarship offer, etc.); he may receive a scholarship after enrolling, and that aid counts against the school's scholarship quota the next year.

A fan or donor connected to a school's athletics; boosters fund NIL collectives, and the new College Sports Commission can bar NIL pay from 'associated entities or individuals', which seems to mean boosters.
A postseason game, traditionally an exhibition between two invited FBS teams; today six bowls host CFP quarterfinals and semifinals and the rest form the postseason for teams outside the Playoff.

The 12-team postseason tournament that decides the FBS national champion; automatic bids go to the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC champions and the top-ranked champion from the other conferences (2026-27).
The organization launched by the power conferences in 2025 that oversees the House settlement rules, the NIL clearinghouse and the revenue-sharing cap, and punishes violations.
A scholarship offer a recruit can accept right away and be guaranteed a spot; an uncommittable offer is one the school may not honor.
The school office that checks the program follows NCAA rules and handles paperwork such as entering a player's name into the transfer portal.
A rating that blends several recruiting services' ratings into one score for a prospect.
The title decided among a college conference's teams; in 2026-27 the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC champions earn automatic College Football Playoff bids.
Schools changing conferences, which reshaped college football (for example the Pac-12 shrinking to two members after the 2023 season).
A recruiting-calendar period when coaches may meet recruits in person, including on campus, at tournaments, at home and at school.
An extra season of eligibility the NCAA granted to athletes who met certain criteria because of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The most restrictive recruiting-calendar period: no in-person contact or visits, though electronic and written communication is allowed.
A recruit withdraws a previous verbal commitment, often to flip to another school.
A player who lost his roster spot to the new roster limits and, as a DSA, does not count against a roster limit at his current or a new school for the rest of his college career.
A recruit who enrolls before the fall semester, often in January, to join the program early.
A signing window before the traditional February date that lets recruits formalize their choice in December (the 2025 cycle began Dec. 4, 2024).
An NCAA-granted exception that excuses an athlete from an eligibility rule, such as a waiver for immediate eligibility after a transfer; most categories are eliminated for D-I and D-II from 2026-27.
A recruiting-calendar period when coaches may watch a recruit play or visit his school, but may not speak with him or his parents in person off campus.
The Football Bowl Subdivision, the top level of college football, whose teams play in the College Football Playoff and other bowl games.
The Football Championship Subdivision, the second level of Division I football, with limited scholarships and its own NCAA playoff.
A player in his fifth year as an undergraduate; under the pre-2026 rules this meant one with five years of eligibility (a 'redshirt senior' was a fifth-year using a fourth year of eligibility).
When a school persuades a recruit committed elsewhere to switch to it.
A rule (FBS and FCS, from the 2018 season) letting a player appear in up to four regular-season games and still keep that season as a redshirt year; historical for D-I from 2026-27.
terms.variants: Division II uses a three-game rule (from 2023)

terms.definition: A player who has earned his degree at one school and moves to another using remaining eligibility, with immediate eligibility.
A recruit who delays full-time enrollment (for example to the winter or spring term) so the eligibility clock starts later; the pre-2026 rules that governed this are replaced by the age-based model.
The six FBS conferences outside the Power Four (American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12, Sun Belt); 'Group of Five' is the older term from when the Pac-12 was a power conference.
terms.variants: Group of Five (historical, still used in 2026 by some outlets)

terms.definition: A request to restore a season lost to injury or other hardship, historically for athletes who got hurt after playing in under 30% of games; eliminated for Division I and II by the 2026-27 age-based rules.

The class-action settlement of House v. NCAA (approved June 6, 2025) that lets schools opt in to revenue sharing with athletes, sets roster limits in place of scholarship limits, and created the NIL clearinghouse.
A transferring athlete may play at the new school right away, without sitting out a year in residence.
A payment, favor or recruiting inducement to a player or recruit that breaks NCAA rules (for example a school paying for unofficial visit expenses).
An FBS school that plays football outside a conference; in 2026 there are two, and Notre Dame is one that may earn an automatic CFP bid by ranking in the top 12.

A two-year college; players can start there and move to a four-year school, and time at one counts toward NCAA eligibility under the pre-2026 rules (and full-time enrollment there starts the new five-year clock).
A binding agreement to attend a school (since 1964) that the NCAA eliminated in October 2024, replacing it with a financial aid agreement.
terms.variants: athletics financial aid agreement; athletic aid agreement

terms.definition: The traditional February date, the start of the traditional signing period, when high school seniors sign with schools (Feb. 5 in the 2025 cycle).
The NCAA's three competitive levels (Divisions I, II, III); in football, Division I is split into FBS and FCS.
The NCAA office that certifies initial eligibility, and from fall 2026 also administers and certifies the five-year eligibility period.
A booster-funded organization that pools money to arrange or fund NIL deals for a school's athletes; some schools are folding collectives into the athletic department since the House settlement.
A player's right to earn money from the use of his name, image and likeness, such as endorsements and sponsorships; allowed nationwide since July 1, 2021.
The online platform, built with Deloitte, through which athletes submit third-party NIL deals above $600 to the clearinghouse for a fair-market-value and valid-business-purpose check.
A school's recruiting signal to a prospect that it wants him, usually with a scholarship; its force varies (verbal, committable, or written).
A campus visit by a recruit that is arranged under NCAA recruiting rules and may include school-provided expenses.
A recruiting and transfer-tracking media service that publishes rankings, a transfer portal wire and NIL valuations; its Rivals brand publishes the Rivals Industry Ranking.
A 2021 NCAA rule that let an athlete transfer once without sitting out a year; replaced in April 2024 by unlimited immediate-eligibility transfers.
A December 2024 federal preliminary injunction for former JUCO player Diego Pavia on how the NCAA counts non-NCAA seasons toward eligibility; the NCAA then gave a blanket extra year for 2025-26.
Paying athletes directly for playing or to recruit them; the NCAA long banned it, and revenue sharing since July 2025 lets schools pay players directly.
The group of transfer players a school adds during a transfer cycle.
A sanction or consequence that bars a team from postseason play; low APR scores can cost a team postseason eligibility.
The four most prominent FBS conferences: ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC (formerly the Power Five before the Pac-12 collapsed).
A non-scholarship player the program invites to join, who often has a clearer roster path than an ordinary walk-on.
A period of added monitoring and restrictions after an NCAA violation (here three years, with limits on visits and recruiting contacts).
A recruiting-calendar period when coaches may not meet recruits or parents face to face off the college campus and may not watch them compete; campus visits are where contact happens.
The group of players a school signs or adds during one recruiting cycle.

A season in which a player practices with the team but plays little or not at all, so the season does not use up a year of eligibility; for NCAA Division I and II this concept is eliminated by the age-based model starting 2026-27 (historical).
terms.variants: redshirt freshman, redshirt sophomore, redshirt senior

terms.definition: Direct payments from schools to athletes, allowed since July 1, 2025 under the House settlement for schools that opt in, up to a per-school cap (about $20.5 million in 2025-26).
A cap on how many players a team may carry; for football the House settlement set 105 for schools that opt in, and each of those players may receive a scholarship.
Financial aid from a school to an athlete for playing a sport; under the House roster-limit model, every player inside a team's roster cap may receive one.
Practice players who simulate the upcoming opponent's schemes for the starting offense or defense.
An NCAA sanction on an individual (usually a coach or staffer) that bars him from working in college athletics until the order expires.
A recruit who has privately committed to a school but has not announced it publicly.
A recruit who has committed to a school but is still considering or visiting other schools.
A recruiting service's grade that groups prospects into levels such as five-star, four-star and three-star.
An NCAA online database of athletes who have said they want to change schools; once a name is in it, other schools may contact the athlete.
A player's formal notice to his school's compliance office that he wants to transfer, after which the school must enter his name in the portal within two business days (SI) or 48 hours (ESPN, On3).
The set dates in which a football player must enter the portal; from 2026 FBS and FCS football has a single 15-day window, Jan. 2-16.
terms.variants: earlier: winter window in December plus a spring window (2024-25: Dec. 9-28 and Apr. 16-25)

terms.definition: A first-year college player who has not redshirted.
A campus visit by a recruit that is not funded the way an official visit is (the recruit's family pays).
Wins erased from a team's record as a penalty for using ineligible players or other violations.
A recruit's public, non-binding promise to attend a school.
A college player who is on the team without having been awarded an athletic scholarship.
The old rule that a transferring underclassman had to sit out a year at the new school before playing, unless he got an NCAA waiver.
